# Generated File Ownership

## Overview

This framework contains two types of files:

1. **Managed files** — Generated by `qaff` and kept in sync across updates. Do not edit these directly.
2. **Custom files** — Your application code. Edit freely.

This document explains which files are which.

## Managed Files

Managed files are regenerated when you run `qaff create` or `qaff update`. Their content is deterministic based on your configuration.

Examples:
- `pom.xml` (root and all modules)
- `framework-*/**` (all framework module code)
- `apps/<id>/*/pom.xml` (app module POMs)
- Generated demo test classes (e.g., `*SmokeTest.java`)
- `.github/workflows/` (CI/CD definitions)

**Do not edit managed files.** `qaff update` renders from `qa-factory.lock.json`; this project ships no config file. To change a setting (manual, review-first):
1. Export the config: `qaff export-config --project . --output qa-factory.yaml`.
2. Edit it and regenerate into a fresh directory: `qaff create --config qa-factory.yaml --output <fresh-dir>`.
3. `diff -rq <fresh-dir> .` lists what changed; copy those managed files, `qa-factory.lock.json` and `.qaff/managed-base/` from the fresh directory into this project. `qaff update --project . --dry-run` reports `CLEAN` once nothing is missing.

Apps and layers change through `qaff add-app` / `add-layer` / `remove-app` / `remove-layer` / `rename-app` instead — they update the lock for you.

## Custom Files

Custom files are created for you to edit. They are never overwritten by `qaff`.

Examples:
- `apps/<id>/web-desktop/src/test/java/**/*Test.java` (your tests)
- `apps/<id>/web-desktop/src/test/java/**/*Page.java` (your page objects)
- `apps/<id>/*/src/test/resources/` (your test data)
- `src/main/resources/application.properties` (your config)

**Edit these freely.** They are never touched by `qaff`.

## Create-Once Files

Create-once files are generated as starter templates and then belong to you. `qaff update` restores one when it is missing, but never reports an existing copy as changed and never overwrites it.

| File | When generated | Who changes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config/zephyr-mapping.json`, `config/xray-mapping.json`, `config/testrail-mapping.json` (or the configured `mappingFile`) | A test-management integration with a `mappingFile` is enabled | You — fill in the test-to-case mappings |
| `framework-performance/baseline/<app>.baseline.json` | The Quality Impact pack is enabled and the app has the `performance` layer | `qaff update-baseline` from a trusted result |

`qaff update-app --force` is an explicit per-app overwrite and does overwrite create-once files; `qaff update` never does.

## Edit-Safe Zones

These directories are safe to extend with custom code:

```
apps/<id>/
├── web-desktop/
│   └── src/test/java/  ← Add your tests here
├── api/
│   └── src/test/java/  ← Add your API tests here
├── integration/
│   └── src/test/java/  ← Add your integration tests here
└── performance/
    └── src/test/java/  ← Add your Gatling simulations here
```

And:

```
framework-web/
└── src/test/java/  ← Add shared page objects here
```

## Checking Ownership

Run `qaff update --project . --dry-run` to see which managed files differ from the renderer output for your lock.

If a managed file was edited:
1. Save your changes to a separate file
2. Run `qaff update --project . --apply --accept-renderer` to restore the file (plain `--apply` keeps locally modified files and writes sidecars for conflicts; `--merge-conflicts` attempts a three-way merge instead; `--paths <list>` limits the run)
3. Manually re-apply your changes if needed
4. Consider whether your change should be in config instead
